prerequisites: It is recommended to have passed the first-year subject of Graphic Expression.
It is recommended to have passed the first-year subject of Graphic Expression and CAD.

learning_outcomes.text: Will know the most common components involved in mechanisms and their standardized representation.
Will develop the skill to draw, according to standard, mechanisms formed by several assembled components, as well as the assembly representation and manufacturing representation of the components.
Will develop the skill and proficiency in the use of manual and computer-aided drawing tools.
Will carry out a project in a real way.

Will be able to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, as well as communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of industrial engineering.
Will develop the skill and proficiency for decision-making in the field of industrial engineering through the study of data obtained by combining graphic and written language.
Will have acquired the skill and proficiency to correctly reflect decisions in the field of industrial engineering, through the study of data obtained by combining graphic and written language.
Will have acquired teamwork, project design, and development competencies.
Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Mechanical Industrial Engineering.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Ability to work effectively in a team.
Ability to design and develop projects.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Assembly and Detail Drawings
Gears, Bearings, Springs, Belts and Chains
Specific Representations of Machine and Mechanisms
Drawings of an Industrial Engineering Project
teaching_methods: Practical classes in the classroom (exercises on paper)
Autonomous work (quizzes and forums on Virtual Classroom)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance to theoretical and laboratory practical classes

assessment_rules: To pass continuous assessment, students must attend at least 80% of theoretical and practical classes, submit at least 80% of weekly practical assignments on time, submit and pass the group project, and pass all continuous assessment tests with an average of over 5 points (each test score must be 5 points or higher). Failure in any of these conditions, or not participating in at least 50% of activities, results in a failing grade of 4.0. For students who did not pass continuous assessment or opt for single assessment, the final grade is calculated as 20% for weekly practical assignments, 20% for the group project, and 60% for the final exam. The final exam consists of a theoretical part (40%) and a practical part (60%), both requiring a score of 5 points or higher to be averaged, and the overall exam average must be over 5 points to pass. Grades are not carried over between academic years.
